initial_units.coptic_label: Diplomatic opening (Codex II, p. 32 — after Coptic Scriptorium NHAM.02)
initial_units.english: These are the secret sayings that the living Jesus spoke and Didymus Judas Thomas wrote down.
initial_units.english_label: English of this logion
initial_units.english_source: Display rendering aligned to Coptic Scriptorium diplomatic (not Lambdin/Robinson copyrighted editions)

initial_units.coptic_label: Diplomatic excerpt, logion 2 opening
initial_units.english: Jesus said: Let one who seeks continue seeking until he finds. When he finds, he will be troubled, and when he is troubled he will marvel and will reign over the All.
initial_units.english_label: English of this logion
initial_units.english_source: Display rendering; Greek overlap in P.Oxy. 654 follows Grenfell & Hunt 1904 (PD) where applicable

initial_units.coptic_label: Diplomatic excerpt, logion 3 opening
initial_units.english: Jesus said: If those who lead you say to you, 'See, the kingdom is in heaven,' then the birds of heaven will precede you.
initial_units.english_label: English of this logion
initial_units.english_source: Display rendering aligned to diplomatic Coptic

nhc-ii-gospel-thomas.attribution: Coptic diplomatic (Gospel of Thomas): Coptic Scriptorium (CC-BY 4.0). Images: Claremont Nag Hammadi Archive (IIIF embed only). English: short display excerpts, not a dumped modern critical translation.
nhc-ii-gospel-thomas.canonical_diff_note: Sayings collection (114 logia) in Coptic, not a narrative Gospel; some parallels to Synoptic sayings but many unique teachings and no birth, passion, or resurrection account.

initial_units.coptic_label: Opening words on Codex II p. 51 (diplomatic excerpt — verify against edition)
initial_units.coptic_source: Seed excerpt; full diplomatic edition not yet bundled
initial_units.english: A Hebrew makes another Hebrew, and such a person is called a proselyte. But a proselyte does not make a proselyte.
initial_units.english_label: English of opening lines on this leaf
initial_units.english_source: Brief display excerpt; full Coptic diplomatic text pending open edition in v1

nhc-ii-gospel-philip.attribution: Coptic diplomatic (Gospel of Thomas): Coptic Scriptorium (CC-BY 4.0). Images: Claremont Nag Hammadi Archive (IIIF embed only). English: short display excerpts, not a dumped modern critical translation.
nhc-ii-gospel-philip.canonical_diff_note: Valentinian anthology of sayings and ritual notes — not a biography like Matthew–John and absent from every major NT canon list.

initial_units.coptic_label: Coptic diplomatic text not yet bundled for this tractate in v1
initial_units.english: On account of the reality of the authorities, the great apostle — referring to the 'perfect man' — wrote to us that 'our contest is not against flesh and blood.'
initial_units.english_label: English of opening lines on this leaf
initial_units.english_source: Display excerpt for leaf context; full diplomatic Coptic pending open license in v1

nhc-ii-hypostasis-archons.attribution: Coptic diplomatic (Gospel of Thomas): Coptic Scriptorium (CC-BY 4.0). Images: Claremont Nag Hammadi Archive (IIIF embed only). English: short display excerpts, not a dumped modern critical translation.
nhc-ii-hypostasis-archons.canonical_diff_note: Gnostic cosmology re-reading Genesis (archons, Sophia); not a Gospel or epistle in the NT genre set.

initial_units.tractate: On the Origin of the World
initial_units.coptic_label: Coptic diplomatic text not yet bundled for this tractate in v1
initial_units.english: Since everyone, including the rulers of chaos and the underworld, wishes to show that the world is a work of their own, it is necessary to declare the nature of the universe and how it came to be.
initial_units.english_label: English of opening lines on this leaf
initial_units.english_source: Display excerpt; not a full modern critical translation dump

nhc-ii-origin-world.attribution: Coptic diplomatic (Gospel of Thomas): Coptic Scriptorium (CC-BY 4.0). Images: Claremont Nag Hammadi Archive (IIIF embed only). English: short display excerpts, not a dumped modern critical translation.
nhc-ii-origin-world.canonical_diff_note: Cosmological treatise with Genesis/Enoch motifs; belongs to second-temple and Gnostic speculation, not the NT corpus.

initial_units.coptic_label: Coptic diplomatic text not yet bundled for this tractate in v1
initial_units.english: Wise men of old gave the soul a feminine name. Indeed she is feminine in her nature as well.
initial_units.english_label: English of opening lines on this leaf
initial_units.english_source: Display excerpt for shown leaf

nhc-ii-exegesis-soul.attribution: Coptic diplomatic (Gospel of Thomas): Coptic Scriptorium (CC-BY 4.0). Images: Claremont Nag Hammadi Archive (IIIF embed only). English: short display excerpts, not a dumped modern critical translation.
nhc-ii-exegesis-soul.canonical_diff_note: Allegorical treatise on the soul’s fall and return; homiletic philosophy, not NT narrative or letter.

initial_units.coptic_label: Coptic diplomatic text not yet bundled for this tractate in v1
initial_units.english: The secret words that the savior spoke to Judas Thomas, which I, Mathaias, wrote down while I was walking and listening to them.
initial_units.english_label: English of opening lines on this leaf
initial_units.english_source: Display excerpt for shown leaf

nhc-ii-thomas-contender.attribution: Coptic diplomatic (Gospel of Thomas): Coptic Scriptorium (CC-BY 4.0). Images: Claremont Nag Hammadi Archive (IIIF embed only). English: short display excerpts, not a dumped modern critical translation.
nhc-ii-thomas-contender.canonical_diff_note: Post-resurrection dialogue attributed to Thomas; revelatory discourse unlike the canonical Gospel forms.

initial_units.coptic_label: Coptic diplomatic text not yet bundled for this tractate in v1
initial_units.english: The teaching of the savior, and the revelation of the mysteries and the things hidden in silence, which he taught John, his disciple.
initial_units.english_label: English of opening lines on this leaf
initial_units.english_source: Display excerpt for shown leaf

nhc-ii-apocryphon-john.attribution: Coptic diplomatic (Gospel of Thomas): Coptic Scriptorium (CC-BY 4.0). Images: Claremont Nag Hammadi Archive (IIIF embed only). English: short display excerpts, not a dumped modern critical translation.
nhc-ii-apocryphon-john.canonical_diff_note: Revelatory “secret book” with a secondary creator-god myth; contradicts the monotheistic theology of the canonical NT.

initial_units.coptic_label: Coptic diplomatic text not yet bundled for this tractate in v1
initial_units.english: The gospel of truth is joy for those who have received from the Father of truth the grace of knowing him, through the power of the Word.
initial_units.english_label: English of opening lines on this leaf
initial_units.english_source: Display excerpt for shown leaf

nhc-i-gospel-truth.attribution: Coptic diplomatic (Gospel of Thomas): Coptic Scriptorium (CC-BY 4.0). Images: Claremont Nag Hammadi Archive (IIIF embed only). English: short display excerpts, not a dumped modern critical translation.
nhc-i-gospel-truth.canonical_diff_note: Valentinian homily on truth and error — not one of the four canonical Gospels and not a Pauline letter.

initial_units.coptic_label: Coptic diplomatic text not yet bundled for this tractate in v1
initial_units.english: Since you asked that I send you a secret book which was revealed to me and Peter by the Lord, I cannot refuse you.
initial_units.english_label: English of opening lines on this leaf
initial_units.english_source: Display excerpt for shown leaf

nhc-i-apocryphon-james.attribution: Coptic diplomatic (Gospel of Thomas): Coptic Scriptorium (CC-BY 4.0). Images: Claremont Nag Hammadi Archive (IIIF embed only). English: short display excerpts, not a dumped modern critical translation.
nhc-i-apocryphon-james.canonical_diff_note: First Apocalypse of James (revelation to James); apocalyptic dialogue, not a canonical epistle or Gospel.

initial_units.coptic_label: Coptic diplomatic text not yet bundled for this tractate in v1
initial_units.english: The teaching of the savior, and the revelation of the mysteries and the things hidden in silence, even those things which were taught John, his disciple.
initial_units.english_label: English of lines on this leaf
initial_units.english_source: Display excerpt parallel to Codex II opening

nhc-iii-apocryphon-john.attribution: Coptic diplomatic (Gospel of Thomas): Coptic Scriptorium (CC-BY 4.0). Images: Claremont Nag Hammadi Archive (IIIF embed only). English: short display excerpts, not a dumped modern critical translation.
nhc-iii-apocryphon-john.canonical_diff_note: Third Coptic copy of the Apocryphon of John (long recension); same non-NT genre as Codex II/IV witnesses.

initial_units.coptic_label: Coptic diplomatic text not yet bundled for this tractate in v1
initial_units.english: The teaching of the savior, and the revelation of the mysteries and the things hidden in silence, which he taught John, his disciple, one day when he was resting upon a bed in the temple.
initial_units.english_label: English of opening lines on this leaf
initial_units.english_source: Display excerpt for leaf context; not a full modern critical translation dump

nhc-iv-apocryphon-john-long.attribution: Coptic diplomatic (Gospel of Thomas): Coptic Scriptorium (CC-BY 4.0). Images: Claremont Nag Hammadi Archive (IIIF embed only). English: short display excerpts, not a dumped modern critical translation.
nhc-iv-apocryphon-john-long.canonical_diff_note: Third Coptic witness to a Gnostic revelation dialogue; not a Greek NT manuscript and teaches a mythic cosmology foreign to canonical christology.

initial_units.coptic_label: Coptic diplomatic text not yet bundled for this tractate in v1
initial_units.english: The holy book of the great invisible Spirit, the Father whose name cannot be uttered, he who came forth from the heights of the perfection, the light of the light of the aeons of light.
initial_units.english_label: English of opening lines on this leaf
initial_units.english_source: Display excerpt for leaf context; not a full modern critical translation dump

nhc-iv-gospel-egyptians.attribution: Coptic diplomatic (Gospel of Thomas): Coptic Scriptorium (CC-BY 4.0). Images: Claremont Nag Hammadi Archive (IIIF embed only). English: short display excerpts, not a dumped modern critical translation.
nhc-iv-gospel-egyptians.canonical_diff_note: Title says “Gospel” but the work is a Sethian revelation about aeons and baptism — not Matthew–John narrative and rejected by proto-orthodox catalogues.

initial_units.coptic_label: Coptic diplomatic text not yet bundled for this tractate in v1
initial_units.english: The blessed Eugnostos said: No one can see the Father and the Son, nor can anyone know them, unless one receives the Spirit of the Father and becomes entirely Spirit.
initial_units.english_label: English of opening lines on this leaf
initial_units.english_source: Display excerpt for leaf context; not a full modern critical translation dump

nhc-v-eugnostos.attribution: Coptic diplomatic (Gospel of Thomas): Coptic Scriptorium (CC-BY 4.0). Images: Claremont Nag Hammadi Archive (IIIF embed only). English: short display excerpts, not a dumped modern critical translation.
nhc-v-eugnostos.canonical_diff_note: Pagan-philosophical theogony later Christianized in the Wisdom of Jesus Christ; not an NT book or apostolic letter.

initial_units.coptic_label: Coptic diplomatic text not yet bundled for this tractate in v1
initial_units.english: It came to pass when Paul was in the city of Jericho that he went up into the mountain to pray, in order that he might go up to Jerusalem.
initial_units.english_label: English of opening lines on this leaf
initial_units.english_source: Display excerpt for leaf context; not a full modern critical translation dump

nhc-v-apocalypse-paul.attribution: Coptic diplomatic (Gospel of Thomas): Coptic Scriptorium (CC-BY 4.0). Images: Claremont Nag Hammadi Archive (IIIF embed only). English: short display excerpts, not a dumped modern critical translation.
nhc-v-apocalypse-paul.canonical_diff_note: Apocalyptic travelogue attributed to Paul, unlike the canonical Pauline epistles; parallels other non-canonical Apocalypse of Paul traditions, not Romans–Philemon.

initial_units.tractate: Acts of Peter and the Twelve Apostles
initial_units.coptic_label: Coptic diplomatic text not yet bundled for this tractate in v1
initial_units.english: When he had said this, he went away. And we were afraid, for we did not know what he meant when he said to us, “I will appear to you.”
initial_units.english_label: English of opening lines on this leaf
initial_units.english_source: Display excerpt for leaf context; not a full modern critical translation dump

nhc-vi-acts-peter-twelve.attribution: Coptic diplomatic (Gospel of Thomas): Coptic Scriptorium (CC-BY 4.0). Images: Claremont Nag Hammadi Archive (IIIF embed only). English: short display excerpts, not a dumped modern critical translation.
nhc-vi-acts-peter-twelve.canonical_diff_note: Apocryphal acts genre (merchant/Lithargoel allegory), not the canonical Acts of the Apostles or NT narrative history.

initial_units.coptic_label: Coptic diplomatic text not yet bundled for this tractate in v1
initial_units.english: I was sent forth from the power, and I have come to those who reflect upon me, and I have been found among those who seek after me.
initial_units.english_label: English of opening lines on this leaf
initial_units.english_source: Display excerpt for leaf context; not a full modern critical translation dump

nhc-vi-thunder-perfect-mind.attribution: Coptic diplomatic (Gospel of Thomas): Coptic Scriptorium (CC-BY 4.0). Images: Claremont Nag Hammadi Archive (IIIF embed only). English: short display excerpts, not a dumped modern critical translation.
nhc-vi-thunder-perfect-mind.canonical_diff_note: Poetic self-revelation of a goddess-like voice; no parallel in the NT canon’s genres (Gospel, epistle, apocalypse of John).

initial_units.coptic_label: Coptic diplomatic text not yet bundled for this tractate in v1
initial_units.english: The invisible, spiritual Word came forth from the Father and descended upon the holy virgin Mary, and she bore a son, the Christ.
initial_units.english_label: English of opening lines on this leaf
initial_units.english_source: Display excerpt for leaf context; not a full modern critical translation dump

nhc-vi-authoritative-teaching.attribution: Coptic diplomatic (Gospel of Thomas): Coptic Scriptorium (CC-BY 4.0). Images: Claremont Nag Hammadi Archive (IIIF embed only). English: short display excerpts, not a dumped modern critical translation.
nhc-vi-authoritative-teaching.canonical_diff_note: Catechetical treatise on soul, death, and Valentinian soteriology — not a NT epistle and teaches a framework unlike Paul’s letters.

initial_units.coptic_label: Coptic diplomatic text not yet bundled for this tractate in v1
initial_units.english: I am Protennoia, the Thought that dwells in the Light. I am the movement that dwells in the All, she in whom the All takes its stand.
initial_units.english_label: English of opening lines on this leaf
initial_units.english_source: Display excerpt for leaf context; not a full modern critical translation dump

nhc-xiii-trimorphic-protennoia.attribution: Coptic diplomatic (Gospel of Thomas): Coptic Scriptorium (CC-BY 4.0). Images: Claremont Nag Hammadi Archive (IIIF embed only). English: short display excerpts, not a dumped modern critical translation.
nhc-xiii-trimorphic-protennoia.canonical_diff_note: Sethian revelation of Protennoia/Barbelo — high Gnostic metaphysics without counterpart as a canonical NT book.
